English: The national reporting system
What is it?

India has a coordinated system for citizens to report cyber-crime. The Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C) under the Ministry of Home Affairs runs the 1930 helpline for financial cyber fraud and the National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal (cybercrime.gov.in) for all cyber-crime complaints. Complaints reach the police of the relevant state, and financial-fraud reports reach banks and payment providers so they can try to hold money.

What is it?

A complaint on the portal is only as good as the information in it. Before starting, open the evidence register (Module 5) and the intake form (Module 4). The citizen logs in with their own mobile number and OTP. After submission, the portal gives an acknowledgement number by SMS and email: this is the key to tracking.

Writing an actionable complaint
What is it?

An actionable complaint lets an officer act without calling the citizen back. It is neutral (facts, not feelings or accusations), time-ordered, and full of identifiers. It ends with what has been done and what is requested.

Escalation and follow-up
What is it?

Follow-up means checking at agreed times whether each agency has acted, and recording what was said. Escalation means moving to the next level when a route does not respond in reasonable time — always with the earlier references and dates.

Legal quick reference and honest expectations
What is it?

A First Responder does not give legal advice, but should be able to explain, in a sentence, which laws protect the citizen and what rights they have. The new criminal laws — Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) and Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam (BSA) — replaced the IPC, CrPC and Evidence Act from 1 July 2024.
